Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mortensor 0.1.9000 (development of 0.2.0)

Clean break: the 0.1.x interface is replaced (see dev/revamp-plan.md).

Benchmarks

  • New vignette “Benchmarks: how well the pipeline works”: interval calibration of the standard models on data simulated from the Lee-Carter model with Poisson deaths, rolling-origin backtests on four real data sets (England & Wales men, France women, England by sex and deprivation quintile, German Laender by sex), and the behaviour of the pipeline on input tables with 26 typical defects, on small populations and on a table of 288,000 rows. The results are precomputed by dev/benchmarks.R and reported without thresholds. On data from its own model, the 95% intervals of lee_carter() covered 95.9% of the true rates; on the real data 63% to 80%, and the mixture of Lee-Carter and the random walk 93% to 99%.
  • The articles have a section “Benchmarks” with this vignette and the comparison with demography, bamp and StMoMo.

New published models; dependence between groups

Work package E5, implemented from the full papers. All new methods are opt-in; defaults are unchanged.

  • lee_carter(family = "nb"): negative binomial Lee-Carter model (Delwarde, Denuit and Partrat 2007), maximum likelihood with one dispersion parameter; predictive draws are negative binomial. On French data (demography package) the dispersion and drift agree with the paper’s estimates within 1%.
  • apci(): age-period-cohort-improvement model (Richards et al. 2019) with the constraints of the paper, optional P-spline smoothing of the age terms (APCI(S)), and ARIMA forecasts of the period and cohort terms with the paper’s choice of orders. The unsmoothed fit equals a constrained glm().
  • cae(): common age effect model (Kleinow 2015) for several populations, by least-squares common principal components. The paper does not forecast; the period effects follow a multivariate random walk with drift (package-specific). With one population it equals Lee-Carter.
  • saint(): SAINT model (Jarner and Kryger 2011) in the revised version of Jarner and Jallbjørn (2022): a Gamma frailty trend of pooled reference strata and stationary spreads of the target strata, with an optional error-correction model for two sexes.
  • coupled(), mt_couple() and reconciled(dependence = "ecc", template = ): ensemble copula coupling (Schefzik, Thorarinsdottir and Gneiting 2013) gives separate forecasts the dependence of a joint model. Every cell keeps its draws exactly.
  • coda_multiway(): multiway compositional model for subpopulations (Bergeron-Boucher et al. 2018). tucker3(transform = "coda") stays deprecated and names it as replacement.
  • CoDa review against the CoDa forecasting literature: coda() and coda_causes() have no numerical departures from the published methods; their help pages state the jump-off without smoothing (as the authors’ code), the zero replacement of Appendix C, and that the alpha-transformation is not implemented.
  • New vignette “Dependence between groups” (vignette("dependence")): why the dependence between groups matters for totals, gaps and inequality, and how joint models and coupling provide it, with backtests on the ONS deprivation quintiles.
  • The Laender vignette states that the jump-off changes little there.
  • The performance study scripts in dev/ (calibration, tuning, stress tests, the 0.1 regression baseline) are removed; their reports stay.

Testing

  • The performance validation suite is removed: the validation/ directory, its GitHub workflow, the benchmark helpers and the slow tests with thresholds on coverage, CRPS, accuracy and runtime. Forecast performance depends on the data; check it on your own data with mt_backtest().
  • The correctness tests stay: agreement with reference implementations and published values, exact identities, coherence and parameter recovery. Checks of the former suite that were not yet unit tests are now unit tests.

Methods checked against the full papers; new published models

Work package E4. The full texts of papers that were earlier available only as abstracts were read (sources and access in dev/methods-audit.md), and the implementations follow them. Results change.

Corrected to the papers:

  • coda() follows Bergeron-Boucher et al. (2017): the time index is ARIMA(0,1,1) with drift (the random walk is order = c(0, 1, 0)), the common component of the coherent model comes from the mean death rates, deviations are ARIMA(1,1,0), rates from age 80 are a Kannisto model to age 120 (open = "auto"; the regression of the open interval is open = "regression"), and intervals come from the paper’s residual bootstrap. Fitted values and point forecasts reproduce the authors’ code to 1e-9. 95% coverage on England & Wales men 0.888 (0.981 before); on French women the coherent model is more accurate (CRPS 0.0743 against 0.0764; open interval 0.039 against 0.062).
  • coda_causes() has rank, order and drift (Oeppen 2008 used rank 2 and ARIMA(0,2,2)); tucker3() uses the ranks of Russolillo, Giordano and Haberman (2011), c(2, 2, 2), and reports their fit measure.
  • Non-negative reconciliation is the algorithm of Wickramasuriya, Turlach and Hyndman (2020); the former heuristic, which could miss the optimum, is removed. With MinT and fixed nodes, the other nodes take covariances conditional on the fixed nodes. Results agree with a quadratic program to 4e-10.
  • life_table(open = "kannisto"/"gompertz") fits the closure by maximum likelihood, as Thatcher, Kannisto and Vaupel (1998); their published parameters are reproduced within 0.11%, the former least-squares fit was off by up to 82%.
  • coherent_fdm() uses weighted principal components (weighted = TRUE, beta = 0.05), as Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen (2013): CRPS on France 0.0550 against 0.0596, 95% coverage 0.802 against 0.760.
  • mt_ungroup(open_split = "pclm") (default): the exposure of an open grid interval is split by the PCLM of the exposures, as Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers (2015); the stationary split is open_split = "stationary".
  • mt_dm_test(): the equal-weighted cosine variance is that of Lazarus et al. (2018); varestimator = "daniell" gives the test of Coroneo and Iacone (2020), oversized with overlapping test years.

New published models:

  • p_splines(): two-dimensional Poisson P-spline forecasting (Currie, Durban and Eilers 2004), adapted from MortalitySmooth 2.3.4, whose fitted and forecast rates it reproduces to 1e-11. On England & Wales men CRPS 0.035 against 0.071 for Lee-Carter; its life-expectancy intervals are narrow (95% coverage 0.40).
  • cp_splines(): smooth constrained mortality forecasting (Camarda 2019), P-spline forecasts with asymmetric penalties on the rates of ageing and of change; reproduces the author’s code to 2e-11. On French women CRPS 0.066 against 0.085 for Lee-Carter; its intervals hold fit uncertainty only, as in the paper.
  • bohk_rau(): varying age-specific survival improvements (Bohk-Ewald and Rau 2017), Bayesian, with the paper’s forecast limits and quantile draws. On England & Wales men CRPS 0.045 (linear core 0.043) against 0.071 for Lee-Carter, 95% coverage of life expectancy at 30 0.90.
  • stmomo("plat"): the Plat (2009) model as specified in the StMoMo vignette (Villegas, Kaishev and Millossovich 2018); CRPS 3% below Lee-Carter at ages 55-89.
  • nordpred_apc(): the Nordpred age-period-cohort model with a power link and cut trend (Møller et al. 2003), written for mortensor; projections agree with the nordpred package to 3e-8. Its draws hold coefficient uncertainty only and are far too narrow (95% coverage 0.11).

Fixes: quantiles of draws are interpolated as a + w (b - a), so tied draws no longer give a median above the upper quantile; errors of rejected candidate models of the forecast package no longer appear in knitted documents with coherent_fdm().

Documentation: dev/generalisation-plan.md plans experimental generalisations of the deprecated package methods, grounded in verified literature.

Published methods as defaults (audit of package-specific methods)

Every method was checked against its published source (dev/methods-audit.md; article “Methods and sources”). Defaults are now the published methods; package-specific options are labelled “package-specific (reference unknown)” in their help pages; package inventions with a published counterpart in the package are deprecated (they work and warn with class mt_warning_deprecated). Results change.

Predictive draws:

  • Deaths are Poisson given the model’s rates (Brouhns, Denuit and Vermunt 2002). The extra-Poisson layer estimated from in-sample residuals is removed: it had no published source, counted observation noise twice for tucker3() and the functional data models, replaced the posterior predictive of the Bayesian models, and the validation generator added the same noise. stanmomo(family = "nb") uses its posterior negative-binomial predictive. Intervals of models of smooth rates are narrower: 95% coverage of lee_carter() on England & Wales men (ages 30-100, check backtest_ew) falls from 0.746 to 0.632; on simulated Lee-Carter data with Poisson deaths it is 0.944.

Models:

  • tucker3() is centred as in the three-way Lee-Carter model of Russolillo, Giordano and Haberman (2011), without the residual noise layer; experimental. 95% coverage on simulated Lee-Carter data 0.748.
  • Deprecated: product_ratio() (use coherent_fdm()), cause_shares() (use reconciled() over a cause hierarchy with additive = "rates", or coda_causes()), rwd(observation_noise = TRUE) (use arima_series(order = c(0, 1, 1), drift = TRUE), its published reduced form), tucker3(transform = "coda") (use coda()).
  • The Li-Lee AR(1) without intercept clamped at 0.99 and the ridge and SVD fallbacks of lee_carter() for sparse counts are documented and warn.

Combining models and coherence:

  • reconciled(), mt_reconcile(): dependence = "none" by default; the reordering of separately simulated strata ("empirical") is opt-in and labelled package-specific. Aggregate intervals of separate models are narrower: 95% coverage of the England total (ONS, WLS) 0.434 against 0.552. WLS and MinT weights from the base draws, the non-negativity heuristic, fixed nodes and proportional reconciliation are documented with their sources and deviations.
  • reconciled() warns (class mt_warning_hierarchy_exposure) when the exposures of aggregate strata differ from those the hierarchy implies, for example causes of death declared without additive = "rates".
  • recalibrated(scale = "constant") by default (member-by-member post-processing, Van Schaeybroeck and Vannitsem 2015); the power law over horizons is an option. quantity = "asr" standardises as mt_backtest() does.
  • anchored() defaults to the jump-off of Lee and Miller (2001): years = 1, decay = Inf, shrink = FALSE; averaging, linear decay and shrinkage (DerSimonian-Laird) are package-specific options. On the ONS quintiles the default is less accurate than the former settings (CRPS of Li-Lee 0.0708 against 0.0656).
  • Attributions corrected: ensemble(weights = "crps") is package-specific; stacking weights optimise the medians; bootstrapped(type = "grid") is the residual bootstrap of Renshaw and Haberman (2008).

Harmonisation:

  • mt_ungroup(preserve_totals = FALSE) by default (the published PCLM); the rescaling to group totals is opt-in. The open age interval inside the PCLM is iterated to convergence and documented as package-specific. Backtests keep exposure totals when they ungroup exposures.
  • Deprecated: ungrouping methods "hyman_kannisto", "natural_gompertz" and "gam", mt_shape_rates(method = "gam"); mt_disaggregate() defaults to proportional allocation by a standard age schedule (method = "shape").
  • mt_smooth(): the weighted Whittaker smoother with smoothing parameters chosen by GCV per age, and a quasi-Poisson GAM in 1D as in 2D.
  • mt_fill_suppressed(): cells without a total get the truncated-Poisson mean.

Evaluation and derived quantities:

  • mt_dm_test(varestimator = "ewc") by default: the fixed-smoothing test with the equal-weighted cosine variance and t critical values (Lazarus et al. 2018). In simulations under the null (help page; check dm_size), the HLN-corrected test ("acf") rejected in 10-19% of samples at nominal 5% with 7 overlapping origins and horizons 2-5, the EWC test in 4.8-7.4% with 7-16 origins. p-values are larger: random walk against Li-Lee at horizon 1, 0.049 against 0.00015.
  • asr() standardises directly on the age groups of the standard (Eurostat 2013) with asr_groups() and asr_columns(); the former even split of standard weights over finer ages (age_groups = "grid") gave ASRs 1.8-11% too high on French single ages.
  • yll() uses life expectancy at the mean age at death in the interval, e(x + a_x) (Murray 1994): 8.5-9.9% lower with 5-year groups.
  • mt_decompose(composition = "pooled") is labelled package-specific; the estimand of mt_excess() and its P-scores are specified.

Documentation:

  • New article “Methods and sources”: every method with its source and status (published, published with deviations, package-specific).
  • All vignettes use the published defaults and were re-knitted; the package comparison was re-run. Results that changed: in “Choosing and combining models” the Diebold-Mariano test of life expectancy over 16 origins separates only the random walk from M6 over all horizons (p = 0.029); the intervals of Lee-Carter, CBD and the functional data model are narrower (95% coverage 0.69, 0.71 and 0.46). In the England inequality analysis the Lee-Miller jump-off made rate forecasts worse and is not used. In the German Laender analysis Lee-Carter forecasts the East-West gap best. “Your own data” pairs Lee-Carter with the random walk in its ensemble.
  • Warnings of joint models name the message once instead of an example stratum.

Published methods added

Models:

  • coda(): the compositional data model of life-table deaths (Oeppen 2008; Bergeron-Boucher et al. 2017), adapted from MortalityForecast 0.8.1, whose fitted values and point forecasts it reproduces. The coherent model of several populations (coherent = TRUE or common_by) has a common component and stratum deviations that follow AR(1) processes. The open age interval follows the indexes. Validation (checks coda_ew, coda_coherent_fr): CRPS on England & Wales men 0.055 against 0.069 for lee_carter(); coherent model on France 0.077 against 0.080 for li_lee().
  • coda_causes() (experimental): the multiple-decrement form of the CoDa model for causes of death, which add up to all causes in every draw. Less accurate than cause_shares() on simulated causes.
  • lee_carter(rotate = TRUE): rotation of the age pattern of decline as life expectancy rises (Li, Lee and Gerland 2013, as in MortCast); life expectancy at birth stays that of the unrotated forecast. On France, CRPS 1% lower than without rotation 10 years ahead and 2% lower 20 years ahead (check rotation_france).
  • stmomo("m7") and stmomo("m8"): the cohort extensions of the CBD model (Cairns et al. 2009), with gc_order and xc.
  • reconciled(method = "energy_score"): score-optimal reconciliation (Panagiotelis et al. 2023), learnt from the base model’s forecasts at inner origins; it reproduces ProbReco::scoreopt() to 4e-15. In backtests on simulated regions and on the ONS data it was less accurate than WLS (CRPS 11-32% higher), which the help page and the coherence vignette say.

Evaluation:

  • mt_dm_test(): Diebold-Mariano tests (with the correction of Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold 1997) of the difference in accuracy between two models of the same backtest, per horizon, allowing for forecasts that overlap in their test years. Agrees with forecast::dm.test() to 3e-14. Horizons with too few origins for the autocovariances get no test.

Derived quantities:

  • lifespan_variation(): life disparity (e-dagger), entropy, Gini coefficient, standard deviation, variance, coefficient of variation and interquartile range of the age at death, for rates, observed data and forecast draws, conditional on survival to an age at. Adapted from LifeIneq 00.04.09, which it matches to 1e-15 on tables with intervals of equal width. The help page quantifies how much the measures depend on the open age interval.
  • Lifespan variation is a quantity of mt_compare_forecasts(), mt_plot_compare(), mt_contrast() and mt_inequality() (quantity = "lifespan_variation", measure).
  • mt_excess() and mt_plot_excess(): excess deaths, P-scores and the loss of life expectancy against the predictive draws of a baseline model, by age group, stratum and year, and summed over years. Cells with estimated deaths are left out and counted. France 2003: 15,100 excess deaths (95% interval 5,600 to 25,400). Intervals covered the true excess in 97-98% of simulated cases (check excess_simulation).

Vignettes and documentation:

  • New vignettes “Lifespan variation” (France: observed, by age, the effect of the open age interval, forecasts of Lee-Carter, rotated Lee-Carter and CoDa) and “Excess mortality” (France 2003 and 1918, German Laender 2020-2024).
  • “Backtesting and scores” tests the differences between models with mt_dm_test(); “Choosing and combining models” adds CoDa and M7 and a test from 16 origins; “Coherent forecasts” describes score-optimal reconciliation; “Model reference”, FAQ, README and the function map (diagrams redrawn) cover the new functions.

Fixes from a review of the whole package

Data:

  • mt_group_levels() takes numeric total, other and keep levels as labels, keeps an unlisted level named like a group in that group (as mt_relabel() to an existing level does), and refuses a group named like the total.
  • mt_read_gbe() reads values with several thousands separators ("1.023.687") and footers in quotes.
  • mt_fill_suppressed() no longer fills cells of strata published at another age resolution.
  • mt_data() treats NA ages as unknown (distributed) and leaves out rows of unknown period with a warning; factor age bounds use their labels. mt_from_hmd() recognises open ages written as "110+".

Harmonisation:

  • mt_ungroup() keeps an observed first year of life out of the fit (its peak spilled into ages 1-6), works with the spline methods on grouped exposures, and warns when dims = 2 is ignored (mt_warning_ungroup_dims). The spline and GAM methods keep the group totals next to a missing group and above a closed top group.
  • mt_smooth(): cells with missing deaths no longer break the smooth; they stay missing (only the 2D GAM predicts them). Smoothing over time works with a single age group. mt_smooth_check() measures the smoothed cells only.
  • mt_disaggregate(): method = "shape" with a shape of zeros gives a flat shape instead of NaN; missing group rates give missing fine rates.
  • step_shocks(method = "interpolate") removes shock years at the start or end of the training data instead of failing.

Models:

  • Models of observed rates (rwd(), arima_series(), ets_series()) fitted to smoothed rates (step_smooth()) now add the observation noise of the raw rates to predictive draws; their backtest intervals were too narrow.
  • Each stratum is fitted with its own random number stream started from the current generator: fits that use random numbers follow set.seed() with any number of cores (bootstrap results differ from earlier versions).
  • rwd(drift_window = ) with observation_noise = TRUE no longer fails; lee_carter(bootstrap = TRUE) resamples the chosen fitting period; lee_carter(adjust = "e0") with age groups without deaths matches life expectancy again (it could silently leave the index unadjusted); stmomo() forecasts one year; tucker3(), li_lee() and product_ratio() run with a single age group; coherent_fdm() reports groups with fewer than two strata.
  • cause_shares(): predictive draws are those of the total model, with its deaths split between the causes, so the causes add up to the total in every draw; the extra variation of the shares beyond multinomial sampling is estimated as such.

Wrappers and hierarchies:

  • reconciled(anchored(...)) and reconciled(recalibrated(...)) reconcile again (the inner wrapper’s fields replaced those of reconciled()); nested wrappers keep their own fields.
  • Observation noise of reconciled predictive draws is independent across cells: the empirical copula reorders the paths only. The noise had been made comonotone across strata, which widened the intervals of the aggregates (validation de_regions: 95% coverage of the aggregates 0.76, before 0.80).
  • Exposures given for the bottom strata only are summed to the aggregates; a reconciled model backtested on bottom-level data scores the right strata (the draws of other strata had been recycled).
  • Hierarchies of one variable are reconciled on the scale of deaths when the exposures of the parts add up to the total, on the scale of rates when each part has the total’s exposure (causes of death).
  • ensemble(): inner backtests are matched cell by cell, components that forecast different strata are refused, and the ensemble fit no longer carries the first component’s calibration or jump-off. Ensembles and tuned() add observation noise according to their components.
  • stratified() with a level named other, recalibrated(seed = NULL), bootstrapped(tuned(...)), mt_coherence() with one year or one draw, and the component of each draw after reordering are fixed.
  • mt_hierarchy() checks its groups; mt_aggregate_strata() warns about members missing from the data. mt_tune() refuses ungrouped data with the reason.

Evaluation and derived quantities:

  • Backtests floor the predictive deaths at half a death after summing them to the observed cells, not per grid cell: with ungrouping inside the fit (step_ungroup()), the floor per single year had biased the scores of age groups with few deaths. Predictive draws may now hold zero deaths.
  • Life expectancy and ASR in backtests are computed from the predictive deaths like the observed values, and only for years whose cells cover the whole age range.
  • mt_backtest() refuses data whose deaths were ungrouped with mt_ungroup() (mt_error_ungrouped_data): use step_ungroup(). Test data are summed to the age groups of a fit with step_regroup().
  • mt_compare() chooses the default origins once for all models; mt_score_table() keeps a model that lacks one target and separates preprocessing pipelines for every target.
  • life_table(): a rate of 0 in the open interval uses the last positive rate (instead of an infinite life expectancy).
  • mt_inequality() leaves the total and groups of a stored hierarchy out of the default order.
  • Plots: mt_plot_compare() with one year, mt_plot_contrast() with other probabilities, mt_plot_age() with unsorted probs.

Vignettes:

  • The precomputed vignettes are re-knitted. With observation noise independent across cells, their backtests show that the intervals of life expectancy are too narrow for every model, most for national totals; the texts say so. In the German Laender, the ensemble of Lee-Carter and the coherent fdm now also forecasts the East-West gap best (with Lee-Carter).
  • “Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp”: the effects plot leaves out the R-hat rows of mt_parameters(), which get their own table; the MCMC fits are seeded.
  • The README and the function map article show their diagrams as images (drawn from dev/diagrams/*.mmd by dev/diagrams/render.js), because the GitHub mobile app does not draw Mermaid diagrams; the website no longer loads Mermaid.

Engineering

  • mt_parameters() works for ensemble() (the parameters of each component, column component, and the weights), stratified() and tuned(by = ) (column group), also inside other wrappers.
  • mt_backtest() and recalibrated() run each origin with its own random number stream, as mt_fit() does for strata: results of models that use random numbers (bootstrap) no longer depend on cores.
  • coherent_fdm() forecasts about three times faster: the ARFIMA models of the ratios are prepared once per coefficient instead of once per simulated path (forecast::simulate() refits them at every call). The draws are identical.

StanMoMo, recalibration

  • stanmomo() wraps the Bayesian Lee-Carter, Renshaw-Haberman, APC, CBD and M6 models of StanMoMo (Barigou et al. 2023), Poisson or negative binomial; draws are posterior draws of the expected rates, fits warn when the chains have not converged. Validation check stanmomo_ew.
  • calibrated() is renamed recalibrated(), and the vignette “Tuning and calibration” is now “Tuning and recalibration”: in demography, “calibrating” a model often means fitting it, while this wrapper adjusts the forecast distribution of a fitted model afterwards.
  • hyndman_ullah() keeps smoothing the rates over age by default.

Vignettes restructured, models and diagnostics added

  • The vignettes are reorganised: one concept per vignette with a simple model, a model vignette, and two applied pipelines. New: “Choosing and combining models” (implemented and wrapped models side by side, ensembles of any combination), “Ungrouping age groups: methods and diagnostics” (replaces “Data at different granularities”), “Inequality in England” and “Differences between the German Laender” (replace the deprivation, causes, regions and HMD forecasting vignettes). Every step of the applied pipelines is chosen in a backtest of the quantity the question is about.
  • coherent_fdm(): the product-ratio method with functional data models of demography (Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen 2013), with simulated paths, groups (common_by) and hierarchies.
  • stratified(): different models for groups of strata, for example Lee-Carter for all causes and Li-Lee for the causes of death, inside reconciled() with the causes scaled to the all-cause forecast.
  • Backtests score gaps between strata path by path: mt_backtest(contrast = c(var = , ref = )) adds the targets "life_expectancy_gap" and "asr_gap". mt_score_table(hierarchy = ) scores the bottom series, aggregates and total separately.
  • mt_plot_ungroup() compares several ungrouping results (a named list) with three views: age profile against the groups, stability over time, and errors against known single years with the Poisson noise band; mt_ungroup_check() gives the same as a table. mt_regroup(measures = ) regroups only some tables (for example the deaths, to check ungrouping).
  • Help pages no longer quote benchmark results; the vignettes show them.
  • Fixes: StMoMo cohort models now have fitted rates for clipped cohorts (their fitted life expectancy dropped to zero in the last years); a missing rate gives a missing life expectancy instead of certain death; mt_smooth(along = "period") uses Whittaker smoothing by default; errors raised inside do.call() no longer print the whole function; mt_inequality() leaves out levels not in order (such as a hierarchy total); the legend order of mt_plot_shares() is fixed.

Comparing models and forecasts

  • mt_compare() backtests a named list of models (each with its own preprocessing) on the same origins; mt_score_table() shows the scores of rates, life expectancy and ASR side by side.
  • mt_compare_forecasts() tabulates one quantity (life expectancy, ASR, deaths, rates) of several forecasts or of observed data as “median (lower-upper)”; mt_plot_compare() draws them in one figure, also around the jump-off year.
  • mt_plot_backtest_design() shows the training and test years of a backtest; mt_plot_tuning() the scores of a tuning grid.
  • Precomputed vignettes no longer show “plot of chunk” captions.
  • mt_plot_smooth() compares several smoothers in one figure (a named list) and shows rates over age (along = "age"); mt_plot_pit() draws PIT histograms of a backtest.
  • Smoothing over time (mt_smooth(along = "period"), step_smooth()) scales the weights within each age: one smoothing parameter now gives the same smoothness at every age. Before, the ages with many deaths were barely smoothed (effective degrees of freedom 15 of 19 at ages 80+ on the ONS data) and those with few deaths strongly.
  • New concept vignettes, one topic each: “Smoothing death rates”, “Where a forecast starts: the jump-off”, “Backtesting and scores” (with the scores explained); the articles are grouped into getting started, concepts, models, applications and help.
  • Vignette “Tuning and recalibration”: the fitting window of Lee-Carter chosen by a hold-out, the width of intervals calibrated, both checked in a backtest.
  • hyndman_ullah(): when the monotonic spline of smooth.demogdata() cannot be fitted (age ranges starting in middle age), the rates are smoothed without the constraint, noted in the fit diagnostics.
  • mt_tune(): standard errors also for a hold-out of a single stratum (blocks of test years).
  • mt_plot_contrast() draws gaps between strata over time (one or several forecasts, with observed gaps); mt_plot_compare(periods = ) with one year shows medians and intervals per stratum side by side.
  • “Getting started” is one short pass through the main steps; “Coherent forecasts: totals and their parts” (live, no longer precomputed) explains bottom-up, reconciliation and fixed totals with one figure each and a small backtest.

Tuning and recalibration

  • hyndman_ullah() smooths the rates of each year over age with demography::smooth.demogdata() before the decomposition (smooth = TRUE, settings in smooth_args), as in Hyndman and Ullah (2007). Before, it decomposed raw rates, contrary to its documentation, and the model errors that simulate() resamples contained the observation noise that predictive draws add a second time. smooth = FALSE keeps the old behaviour (label “unsmoothed”).
  • mt_tune() and tuned() choose settings by forecast accuracy on the last years of the training data:
    • spec_fun may return list(spec = , prep = ), so preprocessing (smoothing parameter, fitting window) is tuned together with the model (for example the number of components of hyndman_ullah());
    • inner_origins = 1 is a single hold-out of the last inner_h years; target = "life_expectancy" or "asr"; metric = "rmse" for point accuracy;
    • select = "one_se" takes the simplest setting within one standard error of the best; scores carry standard errors, scores by horizon (by_horizon) and the chosen setting;
    • by tunes and fits groups of strata separately (for example by sex).
  • mt_score() reports the root mean squared error of the median (rmse).
  • recalibrated(), anchored() and reconciled() around tuned() failed when forecasting (“No simulate_model() method for model ‘tuned’”): the wrappers rebuilt the base model from its specification instead of the one the tuning chose. Fits now keep the specifications fitted underneath.
  • summary() of tuned fits shows the chosen settings.
  • recalibrated():
    • ages estimates the spread factors (and drift) per age band, for models too narrow at some ages and too wide at others;
    • quantity = "life_expectancy" or "asr" calibrates the intervals of these quantities, which also depend on how the ages move together;
    • n_boot gives bootstrap intervals of the factors (forecasts of stratum x origin resampled);
    • the drift correction of bias = TRUE stays constant beyond the longest horizon of the calibration window instead of growing further;
    • a warning when the factors rest on the forecasts of one origin; the table reports the numbers of inner forecasts and scored values.
  • Benchmark of tuning and calibration (dev/tuning.md, validation check tuning_ew): tuning the fitting window of Lee-Carter on a 10-year hold-out improved forecasts on England & Wales and France; tuning the components and smoothing of fdm the same way did not; calibration brought the 95% coverage of all models close to nominal.

Function map

  • The diagrams of the function map and the README fit the width of the website, and their labels are no longer clipped (Bootstrap’s paragraph margin inside mermaid labels made the boxes too small). Map 1 lists the preparation steps in their usual order and leaves smoothing to step_smooth() inside fits; mt_prep() feeds mt_fit(); the function table lists every exported function.

Changes after the third and fourth applied reviews

Two further reviews (dev/review-applied-3.md, -4.md; an epidemiologist and a demographer working through the vignettes on their own questions).

  • mt_decompose():
    • Strata that are totals of others (mt_group_levels(total = ), a hierarchy) are no longer added to their parts: such a cause or group is refused with a message naming it. Causes passed as groups (levels sharing one population) give a warning.
    • groups needs composition = "radix" or "pooled"; the documentation states when each applies (radix only for membership fixed from the start age, such as sex or education).
    • observed = "fitted" uses the fitted rates for observed years, so that a forecast is compared with its own model; "poisson" adds the sampling noise of observed years. Decompositions of an observed against a forecast year report jump_off, the part due to the observed instead of the fitted rates.
    • pairing = "draw" pairs the draws of two objects (default: independent shuffling). summary(change = ) gives the change of a gap between two years path by path, with intervals.
    • Non-finite draws are dropped with a warning; residuals above the tolerance give a warning. print() explains the components; as.data.table() and mt_export() work on decompositions.
    • mt_plot_decomposition(comparisons = ) selects comparisons; titles and axes name the quantity, the unit and the method.
  • Life tables: where n m / (1 + (n - a) m) exceeds 1 (extreme forecast rates), q is 1 - exp(-n m) instead of 1.
  • Reconciliation: method = "proportional" keeps fixed nodes and scales their parts in proportion to their forecasts, draw by draw (top-down, Athanasopoulos, Ahmed and Hyndman 2009). Non-negative projections warn when more than 5% of the draws hold strata at zero or fixed nodes move; $reconciliation$share_draws_with_zeros. mt_plot_coherence() shows the range of the paths.
  • anchored(): the empirical Bayes shrinkage subtracted the sampling variance from the wrong term, so offsets of noisy cells were shrunk too little. ONS Li-Lee anchored: CRPS 0.0654 (before 0.0658) against 0.0666; life expectancy at birth 0.315 against 0.336. summary() of anchored fits shows the offsets.
  • mt_fit() warns when data were smoothed before the fit (raw deaths are then missing and intervals too narrow); mt_backtest() refuses such data (the smoother has seen the test years). Smooth inside the fit with prep = mt_prep(step_smooth(...)).
  • Backtests carry a prep column; mt_score() scores the same model with different preprocessing separately and reports the unit of the scores. print() of backtests with life expectancy or ASR names the other targets.
  • Period axes may have gaps (census years 2001, 2011, 2021): observed indicators and decompositions work on such data; models ask for consecutive years.
  • mt_group_levels(total = ) records totals, which fits and forecast draws carry, so mt_decompose() recognises them.
  • The plausibility warning of forecasts covers the open age interval.
  • The categorical palette has 12 colours (more are interpolated).
  • Vignettes: all-cause forecasts implied by the causes against all-cause models (Wilmoth 1995) in the causes and regional vignettes; proportional reconciliation; decomposition of forecasts (jump-off, the model’s own change, change of the gap, comparison of two models); calibrated Lee-Carter without smoothing in “Forecasting and backtesting”; corrected interpretations and numbers in the deprivation vignette and the FAQ.

Decomposition

  • mt_decompose() splits the difference in a mortality summary between two sets of rates into contributions of ages, causes and population subgroups, as post-processing of observed data (optionally with Poisson draws), forecast draws (draw by draw, so contributions have intervals), or both (an observed year against a forecast year, or two objects). Comparisons: between levels of a stratum variable (var, ref), between years (periods), or between two objects (y). Methods: symmetric Arriaga for life expectancy with causes split by the implied sensitivity (exact), the line integral of Horiuchi, Wilmoth and Pletcher (2008) and stepwise replacement of Andreev, Shkolnikov and Begun (2002) for any quantity (life expectancy, probability of dying, age-standardised rate, or a function of the rates), and Kitagawa’s rate and age-structure components of the crude death rate. With groups, the composition of a population of subgroups is separated from their mortality: as in Riffe, Tursun-zade and Trias Llimós (2024, “Arriaga meets Kitagawa”), with subgroups blended at the radix (composition = "radix"), or for the pooled rates ("pooled", composition effects by age).
  • summary() sums contributions path by path over ages, causes or subgroups; mt_plot_decomposition() draws them as bars, stacked by cause or subgroup, with 95% intervals for forecasts.
  • Results agree with DemoDecomp (horiuchi(), stepwise_replacement()) and LEdecomp (arriaga_sym()) to machine precision on the same life table, and the Kitagawa step reproduces Table 1 of Riffe et al. (2024). New validation check decomposition; article “Decomposing differences in life expectancy” on the ONS data; plan in dev/decomposition-plan.md.

Smoothing, jump-off and fixed totals (methods of the earlier UK analysis)

  • Smoothing over time: mt_smooth(along = "period", method = "whittaker") (one smoothing parameter per stratum, chosen by GCV pooled over ages) and over the age-period surface with a quasi-Poisson GAM, mt_smooth(dims = 2, method = "gam") (te(age, year), about one second per stratum; the 2D P-spline takes minutes). mt_smooth_check() reports how far the smoother moved the data (median absolute log difference, dispersion of the raw deaths around the smoothed ones, variance ratio of year-to-year changes, correlation); mt_plot_smooth() shows observed points against smoothed lines.
  • Models fitted to smoothed data keep the raw deaths (fit$raw_D): observation noise of predictive draws, residuals, observed rates, the MASE scale of backtests and the empirical copula of reconciliation refer to the data before smoothing. Before, noise was estimated from the smoothed rates, which made intervals too narrow.
  • Smoothing over time narrows the intervals of models with a period index; combined with recalibrated() it gave the best calibrated forecasts for England & Wales men (Lee-Carter on the GAM surface, calibrated: CRPS 0.0646, 95% coverage 0.91 against 0.0687 and 0.75). On the ONS quintiles smoothing over time made the forecasts worse.
  • anchored() moves the start of any model’s forecast towards the observed level of the last years (default 3) per age and stratum, with empirical Bayes shrinkage of sparse cells and a linear fade over decay years; ensembles are anchored per component and reconciled models stay coherent. mt_jump_off() reports the step from the last observed and the last fitted year into the first forecast year.
  • Reconciliation with fixed nodes: mt_reconcile(fixed = ) and reconciled(fixed = ) keep trusted forecasts (for example the total, or all causes) and let the other strata absorb the gap. Bottom values that a projection would make negative are held at zero and the rest projected again (a simple form of non-negative reconciliation), so fixed nodes and aggregates are kept; before, zeroed values could move them. mt_coherence() and mt_plot_coherence() show how far forecasts are from adding up.
  • Backtests score derived quantities: mt_backtest(quantities = c("life_expectancy", "asr")) adds rows with target, and mt_score(target = ) scores them; mt_plot_scores(by = "model") draws a bar chart of models.
  • lee_carter(adjust = c("dt", "dxt", "e0", "none")) re-estimates the period index as in demography::lca(), and choose_period = TRUE fits the longest recent period with a linear index (Booth, Maindonald and Smith 2002); ensemble(top_k = ) keeps the best components of the inner backtest; mt_tune(strategy = "two_stage") searches a coarse grid first.
  • Disaggregation: tail ("kannisto" or "gompertz") and tail_width for the open interval in mt_ungroup(method = "gam"); in mt_disaggregate(), year-specific shapes from mt_shape_rates(), mt_disaggregate_check() and mt_plot_disaggregation().
  • Vignettes: “Forecasting and backtesting with HMD data” (chosen period, anchoring, smoothing with calibration, scores of life expectancy), “Forecasting mortality by deprivation quintile” (smoothing check, jump-off, backtests of anchoring and smoothing), “Coherent forecasts” (coherence plot, a fixed total), “Causes of death by deprivation” (causes reconciled to a fixed all-cause forecast). New validation check smoothing_jumpoff.

Calibration, deprivation and coherence vignettes

  • recalibrated() wraps any model specification (including ensemble(), reconciled() and bootstrapped()) and recalibrates the spread of its forecast draws, optionally also the drift, on the last years (default
    1. of the training data. The base model is refitted at several origins in that window. A horizon-dependent spread factor (and drift correction) is chosen by minimum CRPS, or by the interval score of one central interval (target = "interval"). Observation noise is modelled as in mt_backtest(), and draws of an ensemble get the noise of their component. Reconciled models are calibrated at the bottom level and stay coherent. by gives separate factors for groups of strata. summary() and mt_parameters() report the factors.
  • Backtests (England & Wales men, origins 1996-2001, h = 10): calibration raised the 95% coverage of Lee-Carter from 0.75 to 0.88 and lowered its CRPS by 4%. An already calibrated ensemble was narrowed (0.95 to 0.90) at the same CRPS. Drift correction overfitted on the ONS data and is off by default. New validation check calibration_ew.
  • Ensemble forecasts record the component of each draw ($component).
  • Plot layout of the owner’s earlier analysis as the package standard: theme_mortensor(), scale_colour_mortensor(), scale_fill_mortensor(), mt_palette() (ordered red-yellow-green scale for levels such as Q1-Q5, distinct colours otherwise). Forecast plots show observed points, fitted lines (stored in the draws as $fitted), dashed forecast medians with interval ribbons and a dotted line before the first forecast year; mt_plot_forecast() has panels of age by stratum and new arguments colour and log_values; levels defaults to 0.95. fitted() works for ensembles (weighted geometric mean of the components).
  • mt_inequality() weights observed years by their own populations (it used the last year’s for every year).
  • Documentation review: corrected vignette titles and cross-references, Model reference (series models, calibration, sources of uncertainty of every model), FAQ, mt_validate() checks, help pages of ensemble(), reconciled(), cause_shares() and the derived quantities.
  • Vignettes “Forecasting mortality by deprivation quintile” (ONS: inequality indicators, backtests by quintile, calibration, gap forecasts by model, fitting period) and “Coherent forecasts: what reconciliation changes” (ONS sex x quintile with totals: incoherence of separate forecasts, each reconciliation method’s effect on forecasts, intervals and backtest accuracy per level, dependence between strata). The regional vignette adds forecasts for every Land and compares the reconciliation methods on them.

Changes after two applied reviews and stress tests

  • Renamed for clarity: model wrappers are nouns like the other model constructors, ensemble(), reconciled(), tuned(), bootstrapped() (were mt_ensemble(), mt_reconciled(), mt_tuned(), mt_bootstrap()); mt_order_strata() (was mt_cohere()); mt_parameters() replaces lc_parameters() and apc_effects(); mt_window() is internal (mt_subset(periods = )).

  • Hierarchies: additivity per variable (mt_hierarchy(region = "DE", cause = list(total = "all", additive = "rates"))); exposures of crossed region-by-cause hierarchies are summed over regions and taken once over causes in aggregation, validation and reconciliation. Before, all-cause exposures were multiplied by the number of causes.

  • mt_fill_suppressed() takes the bounds of suppressed counts (lower, upper), also without published totals; it stops when no total of the hierarchy is in the data and leaves uncovered cells missing (before, they kept the exposures as starting values).

  • Inspection: summary() of fits (model, sources of uncertainty, fit), mt_parameters() for Lee-Carter, Li-Lee, product-ratio, random walks and Bayesian APC models (with R-hat), fitted(), residuals(), mt_plot_residuals().

  • Results: mt_observed() and observed indicators (life_expectancy(), asr(), prob_dying() accept data, with Poisson intervals), mt_contrast() (differences and ratios between strata, path by path), mt_inequality() (slope and relative index of inequality), life_expectancy(paths = TRUE), asr(per = ) with ages, standard and per columns, standards "esp1976" and "who2000", mt_export() for any table.

  • Future exposures (mt_deaths(), mt_forecast(), mt_reconcile(), mt_aggregate_draws()) are matched by age, year and stratum names and can be mt_data objects; unnamed arrays give a warning.

  • Data input: broader age labels ("1 to 4", "85 years and over", "90 & over", German labels), financial years ("2001/02"), total rows left out and unknown ages distributed with warnings, thousands separators and decimal = ",", trimmed labels, warnings for levels that differ between tables, detection of total levels among the parts, mt_relabel(), mt_regroup(age = "common"); mt_as_exposure() needs an explicit type; mt_read_genesis() makes no analysis decisions.

  • Errors name the missing periods, strata or cells and the likely cause; duplicates name unused columns; overlapping age groups and rates above 1 are located.

  • Robustness: Lee-Carter handles age groups without deaths and sparse counts (ridge fallback); failed strata give one warning; forecasts with rates above 1 give a warning; rwd(observation_noise = TRUE) pools the level variance over ages where deaths are few; smoothing leaves age 0 out and respects group widths; models with one age group work.

  • Backtests: n_origins origins with complete horizons, seeded PIT, estimated cells not scored by default (score_estimated).

  • step_window() (fitting period), as_demogdata(), as_stmomodata(), plots with the original data (data), stratum selection and facets for life expectancy, share plots that take their defaults from the hierarchy, a warning when both h and to are given.

  • Documentation: reference index by analysis step, a function map with workflow diagrams, the “Model reference” vignette, a model-choice table and an aggregation table in the FAQ, no references to 0.1 or internal files in help pages.

  • Data layer: mt_axis (single_ages(), age_groups(), single_years(), parse_age_labels()), mt_data() with tables at their own resolution, mt_grid()/mt_set_grid(), mt_array(), mt_granularity(), mt_validate() (including hierarchy sums), mt_regroup(), mt_operator(), mt_as_exposure(), as_mt_data() for data frames, StMoMoData and demogdata, and the simulated mt_example().

  • Native penalized composite link model and mt_ungroup(): deaths are ungrouped as rates with exposures as offset; the open interval is expanded to omega; 1D (default) and 2D; group totals preserved.

  • mt_smooth() and preprocessing pipelines (mt_prep(), step_*()) that backtests refit on every training window.

  • Interval-aware life_table() and life_expectancy() (also path by path on forecast draws).

  • Model contract (mt_fit(), mt_forecast(), mt_draws) with models rwd(), lee_carter() (Poisson and SVD; agrees with StMoMo and demography), tucker3() (native HOOI; log and CoDa), arima_series(), ets_series(), and ensemble().

  • apc_bayes(): seamless wrapper of the bamp package (Bayesian age-period-cohort models) with convergence checks and draws on the grid.

  • Plots (mt_plot_*(), ggplot2), HMD readers (mt_from_hmd(), mt_read_hmd()), and four vignettes using HMD data.

  • Ports of the 0.1 models and methods: hyndman_ullah(), stmomo() (APC, CBD, RH, M6, LC), li_lee(), product_ratio(), cause_shares() (Tucker4-ILR multi-cause forecasts), mt_reconcile() (MinT, WLS, OLS), mt_order_strata(), stacking weights in ensemble(), Whittaker and GAM smoothing, Kannisto closure in life_table(), monotone splitting of deaths, and the simulated multi-cause dataset mt_example_causes().

  • Grouped hierarchies for coherent forecasts (for example sex x region x deprivation quintile): mt_hierarchy(), mt_aggregate_strata(), multi-variable hierarchy checks in mt_validate(), mt_reconcile() on the death scale with WLS, MinT, structural, OLS or bottom-up reconciliation, an empirical copula for separately fitted strata and non-negativity; reconciled() for reconciliation inside fits and backtests; mt_aggregate_draws(); li_lee(common_by = "sex"); simulated mt_example_regions() and a vignette.

  • Rate-based spline ungrouping (mt_ungroup(method = "hyman_kannisto"), "natural_gompertz", "gam"), mt_disaggregate() for forecast draws, bootstrapped() (parameter and preprocessing uncertainty by Poisson resampling and refitting) and information-criterion rank selection in tucker3(ranks = "bic").

  • “Frequently asked questions” vignette; vdiffr snapshot tests of all plots; Tucker factor signs are fixed so that fits are identical across LAPACK builds.

  • Vignettes “Getting started” and “Causes of death by deprivation” use ons_data; the 0.1-to-0.2 migration vignette is removed.

  • li_lee() and product_ratio() gain jump_off = "observed"; Lee-Carter labels name their variant (SVD, observed jump-off, bootstrap).

  • asr() and prob_dying() return the values of every path with paths = TRUE; mt_plot_shares() gains groups and causes filters.

  • General preprocessing replaces the dataset-specific readers (mt_read_ons() is removed): mt_data() reads text values with symbols for suppressed or missing cells (missing, zero), wide tables with one value column per level of a stratum variable (one column per sex or cause), and tables without some stratum columns, which are shared over their levels (populations shared by causes of death). mt_group_levels() adds an aggregation layer to any stratum variable (cause groups, deciles to quintiles, districts to regions) with summed or shared exposures, a residual group (other, or the total minus the groups) and a new name for the layer. mt_subset() restricts strata, ages and periods. mt_regroup(age = "deaths") aggregates to the age groups of a table.

  • The default modelling grid is the coarsest grid on which every table is exact (the age groups of the data when all tables share them), so models fit grouped data directly; mt_ungroup() ungroups to single years by default (new argument age). The error for deaths coarser than the grid names both remedies.

  • Fixed: reconciled predictive draws of rate-additive hierarchies (causes) returned aggregated deaths instead of rates; the European Standard Population weights of 95+ were dropped for an open 90+ grid group; smoothing of 5-year age groups failed because of singular starting values.

  • rwd(observation_noise = TRUE): random walk with drift plus noise (local level model); sharper than the plain random walk. Interval calibration of random walks, Lee-Carter and ensembles on simulated, HMD and ONS data is documented in dev/calibration.md; the defaults stay.

  • ons_data: deaths by cause and populations by sex, age group and IMD decile, England 2001-2019 (ONS ad hoc release 3064, Open Government Licence), with the cause groups ons_cause_groups; built by data-raw/ons_data.R.

  • German regional data: de_deaths (deaths by Land, sex, age group and ICD-10 chapter, 1998-2024, GBE-Bund) and de_population (31 December populations, GENESIS-Online), Datenlizenz Deutschland by-2-0; mt_read_gbe() parses GBE-Bund exports, and mt_fill_suppressed() estimates suppressed death counts by raking them to the published totals. mt_as_exposure(type = "dec31") for populations on 31 December. Missing cells are reported by mt_validate().

  • Ensembles draw one component per path for all strata (before, components were picked separately per stratum, which broke the dependence between strata and the coherence of reconciled components); every model type is tested as a component.

  • mt_read_genesis() reads deaths and 31 December populations in the flat CSV format of GENESIS-Online (Destatis); parse_age_labels() understands the German age labels.

  • apc_select() (DIC-based choice of random-walk orders for apc_bayes()), and the plots mt_plot_tucker(), mt_plot_shares() and mt_plot_scores().

  • mt_tune() and tuned(); prob_dying(), asr() (ESP 2013), yll(), mt_export().

  • mt_backtest() (rolling origin, scored at the observed resolution) and mt_score() (CRPS, WIS, coverage, PIT, MASE).

  • Validation pipeline in validation/ and GitHub workflows for R CMD check (R 4.3 to devel), coverage, lint and validation.

  • Dependencies reduced to data.table and Matrix (plus base packages).

mortensor 0.1.1

Maintenance release before the 0.2 rewrite (see dev/implementation-plan.md).

  • %||% is imported from rlang, so the package works on R < 4.4 (review D1).
  • forecast() and accuracy() are the generics from the generics package (re-exported); methods dispatch correctly after library(forecast) (D2).
  • Licence changed to GPL-3.
  • Undefined global variables declared; stray files removed from the repository.
  • dev/baseline/ records point forecasts of every model as a regression baseline for the rewrite.
